issue_request: FHIR-7802 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue from DSTU1 asking tooling to catch profiles that weaken a base required terminology binding to extensible, preferred, or example.
initial_application: Jira records the application as svn revision 5953. Git commit 89942b0b07df756077361ad35a65da4870e169d7 imported that revision as '#7802- detect illegal binding in profiles' and added ProfileUtilities warning logic plus publisher plumbing in the old Java tooling.
additional_context: Current source/profiling.html retains the binding-strength change table: required base bindings can only remain required in derived profiles, and constraining profiles cannot make codes valid that are invalid in the base profile. The current Gradle build uses the external org.hl7.fhir:kindling publisher artifact and the old tools/java source tree changed in 2015 is absent from this checkout. Later Zulip and Vocabulary/FHIR-I minutes continue to confirm that derived bindings must be the same strength or narrower.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative profiling guidance is already present, the historical tooling application is in repository history, and there is no current in-repository tooling source corresponding to the old r5953 patch to update.
